    11	/-!
    12	# Arbitrary complex period lattices
    13	
    14	The analytic uniformization theorem starts with an arbitrary lattice in the
    15	complex tangent space.  The earlier `ComplexTorusUniformization` interface is
    16	deliberately tied to the canonical rectangular lattice used for the explicit
    17	torus model.  This file keeps the analytic boundary separate: a
    18	`ComplexLatticeExponentialData` certificate records an arbitrary full
    19	`ℤ`-lattice, its continuous surjective exponential, and the kernel identity.
    20	The topological consequences that follow from these data are proved here;
    21	holomorphic and complex-manifold structure is not asserted without a suitable
    22	mathlib interface.
    23	-/
    24	
    25	set_option autoImplicit false
    26	
    27	namespace Mumford
    28	namespace Uniformization
    29	
    30	noncomputable section
    31	
    32	/-- Analytic exponential data with an arbitrary full period lattice.
    33	
    34	`IsZLattice ℝ periodLattice` is the realification of the usual lattice
    35	condition on a finite-dimensional complex vector space.  The two lattice
    36	instances are stored in the certificate so that downstream results can use
    37	the data without introducing a global instance for an arbitrary subgroup.
    38	-/
    39	structure ComplexLatticeExponentialData
    40	    (X : Type*) [AddCommGroup X] [TopologicalSpace X] (g : ℕ) where
    41	  periodLattice : Submodule ℤ (GenusComplexVector g)
    42	  [periodLatticeDiscrete : DiscreteTopology periodLattice]
    43	  [periodLatticeFull : IsZLattice ℝ periodLattice]
    44	  exponential : GenusComplexVector g →+ X
    45	  surjective : Function.Surjective exponential
    46	  continuous : Continuous exponential
    47	  kernel : exponential.ker = periodLattice.toAddSubgroup
    48	
    49	namespace ComplexLatticeExponentialData
    50	
    51	/-- The additive quotient certificate carried by the exponential data. -/
    52	def toPeriodLatticeQuotient
    53	    {X : Type*} [AddCommGroup X] [TopologicalSpace X] {g : ℕ}
    54	    (d : ComplexLatticeExponentialData X g) :
    55	    PeriodLatticeQuotient (GenusComplexVector g) X where
    56	  periodLattice := d.periodLattice.toAddSubgroup
    57	  exponential := d.exponential
    58	  exponential_surjective := d.surjective
    59	  kernel_exponential := d.kernel
    60	
    61	/-- The quotient additive equivalence induced by the exponential. -/
    62	def quotientAddEquiv
    63	    {X : Type*} [AddCommGroup X] [TopologicalSpace X] {g : ℕ}
    64	    (d : ComplexLatticeExponentialData X g) :
    65	    GenusComplexVector g ⧸ d.periodLattice.toAddSubgroup ≃+ X :=
    66	  d.toPeriodLatticeQuotient.quotientAddEquiv
    67	
    68	@[simp]
    69	theorem quotientAddEquiv_mk
    70	    {X : Type*} [AddCommGroup X] [TopologicalSpace X] {g : ℕ}
    71	    (d : ComplexLatticeExponentialData X g)
    72	    (z : GenusComplexVector g) :
    73	    d.quotientAddEquiv
    74	        (QuotientAddGroup.mk' d.periodLattice.toAddSubgroup z) =
    75	      d.exponential z :=
    76	  PeriodLatticeQuotient.quotientAddEquiv_mk d.toPeriodLatticeQuotient z
    77	
    78	/-- The lattice has the real rank expected of a complex `g`-space. -/
    79	theorem periodLattice_finrank
    80	    {X : Type*} [AddCommGroup X] [TopologicalSpace X] {g : ℕ}
    81	    (d : ComplexLatticeExponentialData X g) :
    82	    Module.finrank ℤ d.periodLattice = 2 * g := by
    83	  letI : DiscreteTopology d.periodLattice := d.periodLatticeDiscrete
    84	  letI : IsZLattice ℝ d.periodLattice := d.periodLatticeFull
    85	  rw [ZLattice.rank ℝ]
    86	  simp [GenusComplexVector, Module.finrank_pi_fintype,
    87	    Complex.finrank_real_complex, Nat.mul_comm]
    88	
    89	/-- The kernel identity gives a pointwise zero criterion for the exponential. -/
    90	theorem exponential_eq_zero_iff_mem_periodLattice
    91	    {X : Type*} [AddCommGroup X] [TopologicalSpace X] {g : ℕ}
    92	    (d : ComplexLatticeExponentialData X g) (z : GenusComplexVector g) :
    93	    d.exponential z = 0 ↔ z ∈ d.periodLattice := by
    94	  rw [← AddMonoidHom.mem_ker, d.kernel]
    95	  simp only [Submodule.mem_toAddSubgroup]
    96	
    97	/-- Translation by a period does not change the exponential. -/
    98	theorem exponential_periodic
    99	    {X : Type*} [AddCommGroup X] [TopologicalSpace X] {g : ℕ}
   100	    (d : ComplexLatticeExponentialData X g)
   101	    (z w : GenusComplexVector g) (hw : w ∈ d.periodLattice) :
   102	    d.exponential (z + w) = d.exponential z := by
   103	  have hw0 : d.exponential w = 0 :=
   104	    d.exponential_eq_zero_iff_mem_periodLattice w |>.2 hw
   105	  rw [map_add, hw0, add_zero]
   106	
   107	/-- The period subgroup is discrete in the ambient complex vector space. -/
   108	theorem periodLattice_isDiscrete
   109	    {X : Type*} [AddCommGroup X] [TopologicalSpace X] {g : ℕ}
   110	    (d : ComplexLatticeExponentialData X g) :
   111	    IsDiscrete (d.periodLattice.toAddSubgroup : Set (GenusComplexVector g)) := by
   112	  letI : DiscreteTopology d.periodLattice := d.periodLatticeDiscrete
   113	  exact isDiscrete_iff_discreteTopology.mpr
   114	    (inferInstance : DiscreteTopology d.periodLattice.toAddSubgroup)
   115	
   116	/- A discrete period subgroup is closed in the Hausdorff topological vector
   117	   group, so its additive quotient is Hausdorff as well. -/
   118	theorem periodLattice_isClosed
   119	    {X : Type*} [AddCommGroup X] [TopologicalSpace X] {g : ℕ}
   120	    (d : ComplexLatticeExponentialData X g) :
   121	    IsClosed (d.periodLattice.toAddSubgroup : Set (GenusComplexVector g)) := by
   122	  letI : DiscreteTopology d.periodLattice := d.periodLatticeDiscrete
   123	  exact AddSubgroup.isClosed_of_discrete
   124	
   125	/- The Hausdorff quotient statement is kept as a theorem (rather than a
   126	   global instance) because the lattice is use-site data. -/
   127	theorem quotient_isT2Space
   128	    {X : Type*} [AddCommGroup X] [TopologicalSpace X] {g : ℕ}
   129	    (d : ComplexLatticeExponentialData X g) :
   130	    T2Space (GenusComplexVector g ⧸ d.periodLattice.toAddSubgroup) := by
   131	  letI : IsClosed (d.periodLattice.toAddSubgroup : Set (GenusComplexVector g)) :=
   132	    d.periodLattice_isClosed
   133	  infer_instance
   134	
   135	/-- Translation by the period subgroup acts properly discontinuously on the
   136	complex vector space. -/
   137	theorem periodLattice_properlyDiscontinuousVAdd
   138	    {X : Type*} [AddCommGroup X] [TopologicalSpace X] {g : ℕ}
   139	    (d : ComplexLatticeExponentialData X g) :
   140	    ProperlyDiscontinuousVAdd d.periodLattice.toAddSubgroup
   141	      (GenusComplexVector g) := by
   142	  apply AddSubgroup.properlyDiscontinuousVAdd_of_tendsto_cofinite
   143	  exact AddSubgroup.tendsto_coe_cofinite_of_discrete
   144	    d.periodLattice.toAddSubgroup d.periodLattice_isDiscrete
   145	
   146	/- The quotient projection is a covering map in the topological-group sense;
   147	   the stronger holomorphic covering assertion remains outside this interface. -/
   148	theorem quotient_mk_isAddQuotientCoveringMap
   149	    {X : Type*} [AddCommGroup X] [TopologicalSpace X] {g : ℕ}
   150	    (d : ComplexLatticeExponentialData X g) :
   151	    IsAddQuotientCoveringMap
   152	      (QuotientAddGroup.mk : GenusComplexVector g →
   153	        GenusComplexVector g ⧸ d.periodLattice.toAddSubgroup)
   154	      d.periodLattice.toAddSubgroup := by
   155	  exact AddSubgroup.isAddQuotientCoveringMap_of_comm
   156	    d.periodLattice.toAddSubgroup d.periodLattice_isDiscrete
   157	
   158	/-- The quotient projection is a covering map after forgetting its deck-group
   159	    structure. -/
   160	theorem quotient_mk_isCoveringMap
   161	    {X : Type*} [AddCommGroup X] [TopologicalSpace X] {g : ℕ}
   162	    (d : ComplexLatticeExponentialData X g) :
   163	    IsCoveringMap
   164	      (QuotientAddGroup.mk : GenusComplexVector g →
   165	        GenusComplexVector g ⧸ d.periodLattice.toAddSubgroup) :=
   166	  d.quotient_mk_isAddQuotientCoveringMap.isCoveringMap
   167	
   168	theorem quotientAddEquiv_mk_eq_iff
   169	    {X : Type*} [AddCommGroup X] [TopologicalSpace X] {g : ℕ}
   170	    (d : ComplexLatticeExponentialData X g)
   171	    (z w : GenusComplexVector g) :
   172	    d.quotientAddEquiv
   173	        (QuotientAddGroup.mk' d.periodLattice.toAddSubgroup z) =
   174	      d.quotientAddEquiv
   175	        (QuotientAddGroup.mk' d.periodLattice.toAddSubgroup w) ↔
   176	      z - w ∈ d.periodLattice := by
   177	  rw [d.quotientAddEquiv_mk, d.quotientAddEquiv_mk]
   178	  constructor
   179	  · intro h
   180	    have hz : d.exponential (z - w) = 0 := by
   181	      rw [map_sub, h, sub_self]
   182	    exact d.exponential_eq_zero_iff_mem_periodLattice (z - w) |>.1 hz
   183	  · intro h
   184	    have hz : d.exponential (z - w) = 0 :=
   185	      d.exponential_eq_zero_iff_mem_periodLattice (z - w) |>.2 h
   186	    have heq : d.exponential z - d.exponential w = 0 := by
   187	      simpa only [map_sub] using hz
   188	    exact sub_eq_zero.mp heq
   189	
   190	/-- A continuous exponential with a full lattice kernel has compact range. -/
   191	theorem target_isCompact
   192	    {X : Type*} [AddCommGroup X] [TopologicalSpace X] {g : ℕ}
   193	    (d : ComplexLatticeExponentialData X g) :
   194	    IsCompact (Set.univ : Set X) := by
   195	  letI : DiscreteTopology d.periodLattice := d.periodLatticeDiscrete
   196	  letI : IsZLattice ℝ d.periodLattice := d.periodLatticeFull
   197	  have hcompact :=
   198	    IsZLattice.isCompact_range_of_periodic d.periodLattice
   199	      d.exponential d.continuous d.exponential_periodic
   200	  rw [d.surjective.range_eq] at hcompact
   201	  exact hcompact
   202	
   203	/-- The compact-space instance forced by the lattice-periodicity argument. -/
   204	@[reducible]
   205	noncomputable def targetCompactSpace
   206	    {X : Type*} [AddCommGroup X] [TopologicalSpace X] {g : ℕ}
   207	    (d : ComplexLatticeExponentialData X g) : CompactSpace X :=
   208	  ⟨d.target_isCompact⟩
   209	
   210	/-- The target is path connected because the source vector space is. -/
   211	@[reducible]
   212	noncomputable def targetPathConnectedSpace
   213	    {X : Type*} [AddCommGroup X] [TopologicalSpace X] {g : ℕ}
   214	    (d : ComplexLatticeExponentialData X g) : PathConnectedSpace X :=
   215	  d.surjective.pathConnectedSpace d.continuous
   216	
   217	/-- Connectedness is a direct consequence of the preceding path-connectedness. -/
   218	@[reducible]
   219	noncomputable def targetConnectedSpace
   220	    {X : Type*} [AddCommGroup X] [TopologicalSpace X] {g : ℕ}
   221	    (d : ComplexLatticeExponentialData X g) : ConnectedSpace X := by
   222	  letI : PathConnectedSpace X := d.targetPathConnectedSpace
   223	  infer_instance
   224	
   225	/-- The exponential is an open quotient under the usual Hausdorff group
   226	assumptions on the target.  Compactness supplies local compactness. -/
   227	theorem isOpenQuotientMap
   228	    {X : Type*} [AddCommGroup X] [TopologicalSpace X]
   229	    [T2Space X] [ContinuousAdd X] {g : ℕ}
   230	    (d : ComplexLatticeExponentialData X g) :
   231	    IsOpenQuotientMap d.exponential := by
   232	  letI : CompactSpace X := d.targetCompactSpace
   233	  exact isOpenQuotientMap_of_continuous_surjective_of_locallyCompact
   234	    d.exponential d.surjective d.continuous
   235	
   236	/-- A continuous exponential with discrete kernel is a quotient covering map
   237	    once its target is a Hausdorff topological additive group. -/
   238	theorem exponential_isAddQuotientCoveringMap
   239	    {X : Type*} [AddCommGroup X] [TopologicalSpace X]
   240	    [IsTopologicalAddGroup X] [T2Space X] {g : ℕ}
   241	    (d : ComplexLatticeExponentialData X g) :
   242	    IsAddQuotientCoveringMap d.exponential d.periodLattice.toAddSubgroup := by
   243	  have hdisc : IsDiscrete
   244	      (d.exponential.ker : Set (GenusComplexVector g)) := by
   245	    rw [d.kernel]
   246	    exact d.periodLattice_isDiscrete
   247	  have h := d.isOpenQuotientMap.isQuotientMap
   248	    |>.isAddQuotientCoveringMap_of_isDiscrete_ker_addMonoidHom hdisc
   249	  rw [d.kernel] at h
   250	  exact h
   251	
   252	/-- The exponential itself is a topological covering map under the same
   253	    Hausdorff topological-group hypotheses. -/
   254	theorem exponential_isCoveringMap
   255	    {X : Type*} [AddCommGroup X] [TopologicalSpace X]
   256	    [IsTopologicalAddGroup X] [T2Space X] {g : ℕ}
   257	    (d : ComplexLatticeExponentialData X g) :
   258	    IsCoveringMap d.exponential :=
   259	  d.exponential_isAddQuotientCoveringMap.isCoveringMap
   260	
   261	/- Surjectivity of the exponential transports the divisibility of the
   262	   complex torus target.  The witness is obtained by dividing upstairs and
   263	   then applying the additive homomorphism. -/
   264	@[reducible]
   265	noncomputable def targetDivisibleBy
   266	    {X : Type*} [AddCommGroup X] [TopologicalSpace X] {g : ℕ}
   267	    (d : ComplexLatticeExponentialData X g) : DivisibleBy X ℤ :=
   268	  Function.Surjective.divisibleBy (fun z => d.exponential z) d.surjective
   269	    (fun z n => d.exponential.map_zsmul n z)
   270	
   271	theorem exists_zsmul_eq
   272	    {X : Type*} [AddCommGroup X] [TopologicalSpace X] {g : ℕ}
   273	    (d : ComplexLatticeExponentialData X g) (x : X) {n : ℤ} (hn : n ≠ 0) :
   274	    ∃ y : X, n • y = x := by
   275	  letI : DivisibleBy X ℤ := d.targetDivisibleBy
   276	  exact DivisibleBy.surjective_smul X ℤ hn x
   277	
   278	/-- The arbitrary period quotient is homeomorphic to the target. -/
   279	noncomputable def quotientHomeomorph
   280	    {X : Type*} [AddCommGroup X] [TopologicalSpace X]
   281	    [T2Space X] [ContinuousAdd X] {g : ℕ}
   282	    (d : ComplexLatticeExponentialData X g) :
   283	    GenusComplexVector g ⧸ d.periodLattice.toAddSubgroup ≃ₜ X :=
   284	  d.toPeriodLatticeQuotient.quotientHomeomorph d.isOpenQuotientMap
   285	
   286	@[simp]
   287	theorem quotientHomeomorph_mk
   288	    {X : Type*} [AddCommGroup X] [TopologicalSpace X]
   289	    [T2Space X] [ContinuousAdd X] {g : ℕ}
   290	    (d : ComplexLatticeExponentialData X g)
   291	    (z : GenusComplexVector g) :
   292	    d.quotientHomeomorph
   293	        (QuotientAddGroup.mk' d.periodLattice.toAddSubgroup z) =
   294	      d.exponential z :=
   295	  PeriodLatticeQuotient.quotientHomeomorph_mk
   296	    d.toPeriodLatticeQuotient d.isOpenQuotientMap z
   297	
   298	/-- The topological quotient identification has the same underlying map as
   299	the additive quotient equivalence.  This lets later analytic arguments switch
   300	between the topological and algebraic interfaces without redoing quotient
   301	induction. -/
   302	theorem quotientHomeomorph_eq_quotientAddEquiv
   303	    {X : Type*} [AddCommGroup X] [TopologicalSpace X]
   304	    [T2Space X] [ContinuousAdd X] {g : ℕ}
   305	    (d : ComplexLatticeExponentialData X g) (q :
   306	      GenusComplexVector g ⧸ d.periodLattice.toAddSubgroup) :
   307	  d.quotientHomeomorph q = d.quotientAddEquiv q := by
   308	  refine QuotientAddGroup.induction_on q ?_
   309	  intro z
   310	  change d.quotientHomeomorph
   311	      (QuotientAddGroup.mk' d.periodLattice.toAddSubgroup z) =
   312	    d.quotientAddEquiv (QuotientAddGroup.mk' d.periodLattice.toAddSubgroup z)
   313	  rw [d.quotientHomeomorph_mk, d.quotientAddEquiv_mk]

   315	/-- The canonical exponential data for the quotient by any full lattice. -/
   316	def ofLattice
   317	    (g : ℕ) (L : Submodule ℤ (GenusComplexVector g))
   318	    [DiscreteTopology L] [IsZLattice ℝ L] :
   319	    ComplexLatticeExponentialData
   320	      (GenusComplexVector g ⧸ L.toAddSubgroup) g where
   321	  periodLattice := L
   322	  periodLatticeDiscrete := inferInstance
   323	  periodLatticeFull := inferInstance
   324	  exponential := QuotientAddGroup.mk' L.toAddSubgroup
   325	  surjective := QuotientAddGroup.mk'_surjective L.toAddSubgroup
   326	  continuous := QuotientAddGroup.continuous_mk
   327	  kernel := QuotientAddGroup.ker_mk' L.toAddSubgroup

   329	/-- A compact-space instance for a quotient by a full lattice.  It is explicit
   330	because the lattice is a use-site datum and should not become a global
   331	instance for every subgroup. -/
   332	@[reducible]
   333	noncomputable def quotientCompactSpace
   334	    (g : ℕ) (L : Submodule ℤ (GenusComplexVector g))
   335	    [DiscreteTopology L] [IsZLattice ℝ L] :
   336	    CompactSpace (GenusComplexVector g ⧸ L.toAddSubgroup) :=
   337	  (ofLattice g L).targetCompactSpace

   340	@[reducible]

## Required proof loop

`lean_goal`). After every proof edit, invoke diagnostics or the goal query again

search to investigate candidates instead of repeatedly launching a build.

Do not start iterative proof work with `lake build`: it is a slow, final-boundary
check. Use LSP for the edit loop and reserve `lake build` for the final session
validation (or when a kernel check is specifically needed). When LSP is
unavailable or crashes, record that in the report and use the narrowest fallback,
usually `lake env lean <file>` or a single module, rather than silently skipping
the check.

LSP is sufficient between edits and between separate obligations. Do not run a
module build after every proof or repeat a narrow build immediately before a
configured final build that covers the same files. At the final boundary, run
the configured build once and wait for it. Add an earlier narrow kernel check
only when LSP failed, the change crosses an interface LSP cannot validate, or a
specific elaboration/kernel question must be settled before continuing.

  inspect goals/diagnostics at the edited location before running a full build.
  This is the fastest loop for filling proofs.

  tactic and after each one. Empty `goals_after` = that step closes the goal.
- `lean_diagnostic_messages(file)` — instant errors/warnings after every edit

- `lean_multi_attempt(file, line, snippets=[...])` — test 3–5 **single-line,
  indented** candidate tactics at once and see exactly which close the goal and
  why the others fail. The highest-leverage tool for filling a `sorry`.
- `lean_hover_info(file, line, col)` — type/signature/docs at an identifier
  (point at the first char). `lean_file_outline(file)` — declarations + line
  numbers without reading the whole file. `lean_run_code("#eval …")` — quick
  standalone `#check`/`#eval`/`#print`.
